sections.h2: Which Texarkana is your house in?
sections.html:
Texarkana, Arkansas serves as Miller County's seat, in the state's southwest corner, with Texarkana, Texas right on the other side of the state line. Because the mailing address says Texarkana on both sides of the line, it cannot tell you the state of a parcel, and the state determines the tax, title and probate rules. Everything here concerns the Arkansas side.

Population on the Arkansas side slipped from 29,919 in 2010 to 29,387 in 2020, with 29,123 estimated for mid-2025. Miller County as a whole counted 42,600 in 2020.

For 2020 to 2024 the median owned home was valued at $170,200 and gross rent at $909. Of 11,333 households, 54.7% own. Household income has a median of $45,835.

Moderate prices shape who sells in a hurry. Owners behind on a mortgage, facing repair bills they cannot pay, or inheriting a house with taxes due tend to have little cash and little time. The median is only a survey number, and any single house may land well above or below it.

Most of the city belongs to the Texarkana Arkansas School District, the largest public district on this side, which feeds Arkansas High School. A sliver lies in Genoa Central. For a house near the edge of town, confirm the district against your parcel record before it appears in an ad.

Texarkana has hot, humid summers and about 48.9 inches of rain a year. The land is flat, and Nix Creek is the main drainage, flowing toward the Red River watershed. Sellers who know where water collects on the lot can answer an inspector directly, and mentioning standing water up front beats having it found.

sections.h2: Is your lot in the city or the county?
sections.html:
Parcels outside the city limits follow county rules rather than city rules. These questions come up often here:

  • Is the parcel within Texarkana city limits or out in the county? That decides who issues permits.
  • Is the house in the Texarkana Arkansas or the Genoa Central district?
  • Who holds title if a parent died and nobody opened probate?

The offices listed next can settle each point before you take an offer.

Planning and Zoning is a division of Public Works at 216 Walnut Street, and it handles building permits, special use requests and zoning compliance. Call 870-779-4974 for Public Works or 870-779-4944 for the city planner. Texarkana uses a council-manager system, and the Planning Commission, Historic District Commission and Board of Adjustment meet under the city, with agendas posted on its meeting portal.

The county offices are all at 400 Laurel Street, Texarkana, AR 71854:

County officeSuitePhone
AssessorSuite 100870-774-1502
CollectorSuite 111870-774-1001
TreasurerSuite 104870-774-0003
Circuit ClerkSuite 109870-774-4501

Property tax in Arkansas falls due every October 15. When real estate tax is left unpaid, the parcel can be certified to the Commissioner of State Lands. The collector's office fields redemption questions at the number in the table.

Selling with back taxes works like this: get the total from the collector, hand it to the title company, and the payoff is taken from your proceeds at closing. Acting before certification leaves you more choices.

Whether you or an earlier owner added a room, carport or fence, Planning and Zoning can say what permits are on file. Call Public Works at 870-779-4974 and give the street address. Ask if each permit was closed out and whether any zoning limits on the lot should be shared with a buyer.

Do not guess. Lenders and inspectors ask for permit records, and a cash buyer will discount work that looks unfinished. Answers from the city make your side of the talk stronger.

sections.h2: What to bring when you call the county
sections.html:
All four county offices are in one building, so a single visit can cover several errands. Take the deed and a photo ID, and the parcel number if you have it.

  • Assessor: confirms the owner of record and the value on the parcel.
  • Collector: tells you what is owed and what has been paid.
  • The Treasurer is in the same building if the Collector sends you there.
  • Circuit Clerk: keeps deed and court records, which matters when an estate was never opened.

Note who you spoke with and when. If a title company later asks where a figure came from, you will have an answer.

A cash sale of a Texarkana house tends to go in five steps. You describe the property and share photos or set up a visit. The buyer then puts a written offer on paper for the house in its present state. After you accept, the title company combs the records for liens, unpaid taxes and ownership gaps. You pick a closing date, sign the deed, and receive what remains after any payoff.

Because both cities share a name, double-check the state on every document. A deed, tax bill or insurance record that belongs to the Texas side will not help your Arkansas sale, and mixing them up wastes days.

Heirs who live far from Texarkana can do most of the groundwork by phone. Call the Assessor to confirm the owner of record, the Collector to learn what is owed, and the Circuit Clerk to ask what is on file if the estate was never opened. Arrange for someone local to check on the house, since an empty building draws more trouble than an occupied one.

Once those answers are in, a buyer can often make an offer without you traveling at all, and the title company can send documents for signing.
A deed in Arkansas carries a transfer tax of $3.30 per $1,000. Name the payer in the contract and let the closing agent verify the amount.

sections.h2: Selling an inherited or repair-heavy house
sections.html:
Roof trouble, foundation work or drainage repairs can keep a house from passing a lender's appraisal, so fewer buyers can use a mortgage. Estate houses bring another layer, because somebody has to show authority to sign. When a parent died without a probate case, settle the title question first.

Get the deed, the latest tax bill, permit records and a short list of known problems together. Any buyer will want them, and having them on hand speeds up the offer.

sections.h2: When a cash sale makes sense
sections.html: Owners who want a set closing date, hold a house a lender would not appraise, or manage an estate from far away tend to fit a cash sale. A listing may bring more for a well-kept house, so look at both. Cash Home Buyers buys houses as-is in Arkansas and prices an offer once it knows the property's facts.

faqs.q: Is Texarkana, Arkansas the same as Texarkana, Texas?
faqs.a: No. They are twin cities on opposite sides of the state line, with separate city governments and different state laws. The Arkansas side is the county seat of Miller County.

faqs.q: How many people live in Texarkana, Arkansas?
faqs.a: About 29,123 in mid-2025, based on an estimate. The 2020 count was 29,387.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Texarkana, Arkansas?
faqs.a: $170,200 for owned homes from 2020 to 2024. That is a survey median, not a price for any one house.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Miller County?
faqs.a: Go to the Miller County Collector, Suite 111 at 400 Laurel Street, or call 870-774-1001. Real estate and personal property tax is due October 15.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Texarkana house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers often buy as-is, which leaves the roof, foundation and drainage work to them.
